text:
simon: quick heads-up — ran a smoke suite on the new "zipper" fused-attn kernel with paged-KV enabled and saw a consistent perf *drop* vs baseline. used the usual load (bs=8, seq=1024).

maria: ugh, details? numbers? :eyes:

simon: baseline (old fused v1, no zipper): 11.2ms/token avg. zipper + paged-KV: 15.8ms/token avg. tail latency also worse (95p ~ 28ms -> 42ms). roughly ~40% regression on token throughput.

alex: interesting — did you hit the KV page thrash path? zipper does aggressive QKV packing + epilogue fusion which can increase per-step mem reads if KV pages cross boundaries.

jen: can you paste the profiler output? especially L2/HBM utilization and memcpy patterns.

simon: pasted a trimmed snippet:
```
# run: ./bench_attn --kernel=zipper --kv=paged --bs=8 --seq=1024
Forward 1000 iters, warmup 100
Avg token ms: 15.8
95p token ms: 42.1
CUDA memcpy HtD: 120MB/s
HBM read: 420 GB/s
L2 hit rate: 61%
memcpy spikes ~ every 16 steps (aligned with page boundaries)
```

maria: that L2 hit rate seems low for packed QKV. packing should improve locality but if pages move, fusion makes it worse. zipper's epilogue writes back differently.

alex: filing theory: zipper's fused epilogue writes KV pages back eagerly when sequence mod page_size == 0, causing eviction on hot paths. kernel chooser still prefers zipper for bs<=8 because synthetic microbenchmarks looked good.

jen: can you repro with larger batch? also test forcing non-epilogue fused version.

simon: tried bs=16: zipper reg shrinks to ~10% but still present. forced `--no-epilogue-fuse` gives 11.6ms (almost baseline).

alex: ok that's telling — epilogue fusion + paged KV interaction is the culprit. two short-term options: 1) teach kernel-chooser to avoid epilogue-fused zipper when paged-KV policy enabled and seq%page==0, 2) disable epilogue fusion by default on paged-KV.

maria: also consider batching heuristic tweak: only pick zipper for avg_seq < page_size/2 or when kv residency == hot. otherwise prefer non-epilogue fused kernel.

jen: can we add a cheap microprobe in runtime that checks recent memcpy spikes and flips to fallback kernel automatically? would avoid global policy churn.

alex: yep, add a small sliding window sampler that watches HBM read/writes per-request; if anomaly rate > threshold, downgrade. cheap check: sample every N requests, look at memcpy size distribution.

perf-bot: benchmark run queued: https://ci.example.com/runs/2567 — compares zipper vs zipper-no-epilogue vs baseline (config attached).

ci-bot: artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-ci/attn/1921239876/ — flamegraphs and nvprof traces (zipper, zipper-no-epilogue, baseline).

simon: plan I'll: 1) disable zipper-epilogue for paged-KV in kernel-chooser patch, 2) add sampler fallback (jen help?), 3) run full perf matrix and open PR. any objections?

jen: happy to pair on sampler implementation. I'll prototype an LRU-like sample collector this afternoon.

alex: logging note: add a structured metric so ops can see when chooser downgrades due to KV thrash.

maria: agree. add an eval job to nightly perf to run paged-KV combos — we regressed before because we didn't include cross-page patterns in CI.

simon: cool. I'll open an issue with the perf numbers + job ids and link PRs. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
